description.value:
The chart’s axes define the visual structure of the data and can be customized to match different visualization needs. Both the horizontal and vertical axes support flexible configuration options, allowing you to control how reference lines and labels are displayed.

You can choose to show only horizontal grid lines, only vertical grid lines, or both, depending on the level of visual guidance you want to provide.
The default is, that both axes lines as well as the split lines are hidden.
If you want to display both axes lines and split lines, use the handle method `axesShowSplitLines()`.
To show only horizontal split lines, use the handle method `axesShowYSplitLines()`.
To show only vertical split lines, use the handle method `axesShowXSplitLines()`.
If you want to hide the axis labels, use the handle method `axesHideLabels()`.
To show axes split lines but hide axis labels, combine `axesShowSplitLines()` and `axesHideLabels()`.

title.value: Visible Axes Lines with Hidden Values

description.value: To add icons to axis labels, use the handle methods `axesAddXLabelIcons()` and `axesAddYLabelIcons()`.

The legend provides a clear overview of all data series displayed in the chart. Each item reflects the series’ label, color, and visual style, ensuring users can quickly understand how values are grouped and represented. 

Depending on the selected chart type, the legend adapts its appearance. Line charts display a small line preview showing the stroke style, while bar charts use a solid color swatch that matches the bar fill. This makes it easy to distinguish series at a glance, regardless of the visualization style.
The default position of the legend is top. The legend can be positioned at the top of the chart by using the handle method `legendShow()` or `legendShow({ position: 'top' })`.
The legend can be positioned at the left of the chart by using the handle method `legendShow({ position: 'left' })`.
The legend can be positioned at the right of the chart by using the handle method `legendShow({ position: 'right' })`.
The legend can be positioned at the bottom of the chart by using the handle method `legendShow({ position: 'bottom' })`.

By default, the legend is interactive. Users can click on a legend item to toggle the visibility of the corresponding series in the chart. To make the legend non-interactive, use the *selectedMode: false* option.
The default story demonstrates a basic line chart configuration. The chart is configured via the `config` property, which accepts an object that maps directly to the ECharts option configuration.

The `config` property is the main way to configure the chart. It accepts an object that maps 1:1 to the ECharts option configuration. Assigning a new object to this property will update the chart with the new configuration.

Use the `palette` attribute to apply a Synergy design token color palette to chart series. `categorical` (12 distinct colors for comparing unrelated data series), `sequential-01`–`sequential-07` (10-step single-hue ramps), and `sequential-status-critical/error/info/success/warning` (10-step status ramps). If `option.color` is explicitly set, it takes precedence over the `palette` attribute.

Use `getInstance()` to access the underlying ECharts instance directly and work with its full native API. This is useful when the `config` property alone is not sufficient — for example to listen to ECharts events, trigger actions, or call `setOption()` with custom merge behavior. This example attaches a click listener via the native ECharts API. Click any data point to see the event payload logged to the browser console.

You can use multiple charts in one `<syn-chart>` instance, each with its own configuration. The palette colors or the default colors can be overridden per series item using the `color` property directly on the series object — allowing fine-grained control over individual chart series colors.

**Important:** The `color` property does **not** support CSS variables (e.g. `var(--syn-sequential-05-80)`). This is a limitation of ECharts itself: ECharts renders via the Canvas API, which does not resolve CSS custom properties. To use Synergy design tokens as colors, read the computed hex value first using `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--your-token').trim()` and pass the resolved value instead.

Line charts offer a clear way to visualize trends, changes and directional movements over time or across categories. By connecting individual data points, they highlight patterns such as growth, decline or stability at a glance, making them ideal for dashboards, KPI overviews and lightweight data summaries. 

The component provides flexible styling options that adapt to different visual needs, from straight linear segments to smooth curved lines. Combined with optional symbols, line charts can be tailored to emphasize exactly the level of detail or simplicity required in your layout.
The lines of line series can be hidden. When hidden, only the symbols remain, which is useful for minimal or simplified data displays.

The line series supports a variety of styles, including line width and line type (solid, dashed, dotted). When combining multiple line charts, ensure there’s sufficient visual differentiation, for example, by using distinct line styles.
The line series supports a variety of symbols.
The line series supports curved lines. Use the `smooth` property to enable smooth curves for the line series.
The line widths and symbol sizes can be adjusted to the needs.
The colors of the lines and symbols can be customized.

The tooltip provides contextual information when users hover or focus on data points within a chart. It displays values, labels without obstructing the view of the visualization. Use the `tooltipShow` preset to enable the tooltip.
Line charts can display both positive and negative values.

title.value: Line Chart with Positive and Negative Values

description.value: Zooming and panning allow users to focus on specific areas of a chart, especially when dealing with large datasets or dense series. The `dataZoom` option provides two types of zooming: integrated zooming and slider zooming. Integrated zooming enables direct interaction within the plotting area, while slider zooming allows users to define a specific data zoom level using handles and a selection bar.

When having large data sets or dense series where users need to inspect local trends without leaving the chart context, the `dataZoom` option with `type: 'inside'` can be used. It enables direct interaction inside the plotting area: 

- mouse drag to pan

- mouse wheel to zoom

 There are possibilities to customize the zooming behavior, for example, to restrict zooming to a specific axis, to set minimum and maximum zoom levels or to add an additional key for zooming. For more information have a look at the [ECharts documentation](https://echarts.apache.org/en/option.html#dataZoom-inside)

The data zoom slider (the `dataZoom` option with `type: 'inside'`) allows users to define a specific data zoom level within a chart by dragging the left and right handles or moving the entire selection bar. It's commonly used in dashboards and analytics tools to filter, zoom, or focus on a subset of data without losing context of the full dataset. The component consists of three interactive elements: 

- Left handle: Defines the start of the selected zoom

- Right handle: Defines the end of the selected zoom

- Selection bar (center): Moves the entire zoom without changing its width

The slider can be customized in terms of position, size and appearance. For more information have a look at the [ECharts documentation](https://echarts.apache.org/en/option.html#dataZoom-slider)

accessibility: Do not rely on color alone to distinguish data series; use labels, markers, or patterns where helpful.
Provide a text alternative or data table for users who cannot interpret visualizations reliably.
Ensure chart context is available in surrounding text, including what is shown and why it matters.

content: Use charts when visual pattern recognition (trends, peaks, outliers) is more helpful than raw tables.
Keep the chart goal specific and clear (for example trend over time, comparison, distribution).
Avoid using charts when exact value lookup is the primary task; provide a table or value list as a complement.
usageGuidelines.name: Data and Purpose

content: Use clear axis labels, units, and legends so users can understand the data context immediately.
Limit the number of simultaneously visible series to reduce visual noise.
Choose palettes that maintain sufficient contrast between series and background.
Avoid excessive decoration and effects that do not add analytical value.
usageGuidelines.name: Visual Clarity

content: Ensure labels, tooltips, and legends remain readable at small viewport sizes.
Prevent overlapping labels and crowded markers by simplifying or reducing displayed data where needed.
Keep chart dimensions appropriate for the amount and complexity of the data shown.
usageGuidelines.name: Responsiveness and Density

useCases: Display time-based trends such as sensor values, throughput, or production metrics.
Compare multiple data series in dashboards to identify differences and anomalies.
Present historical data to support analysis, reporting, and decision-making.
Visualize key performance indicators where users need a fast visual overview.

custom.summary: The `<syn-chart>` component is a container for displaying charts. It provides a structured layout and styling for chart elements, allowing for consistent presentation across different types of charts. The chart component is based on [Apache ECharts](https://echarts.apache.org)
